note: The declared test coverage of the Node workspaces, checked against disk by test-inventory.mjs on every `npm test`. Four of these run jest with no test files and pass on --passWithNoTests; without this ledger that would be a green suite hiding the fact that nothing was checked, which is the pattern this repository keeps removing. Changing a number here is a deliberate act: adding the first test to a workspace fails the suite until the ledger agrees, and so does losing one.
scope: Only npm workspaces appear here, because only these are what `npm test` runs. The Go modules in go.work (go-internalauth, decision-engine, market-data, scoring-engine, signer) have no package.json, are not workspaces, and are covered by `make test-go`, which prints its own passed/failed/skipped count per module. decision-engine has 50 Go tests and market-data 8; scoring-engine and signer have none, and signer having none is uncomfortable given it holds the master seed — it is covered instead by signer-verify.mjs and signer-isolation-verify.sh, which test its refusals and its process isolation rather than its functions.

packages/auth.why: Shared auth helpers. This one already passed --passWithNoTests before, so nothing about it changed. The coverage it lacks is the JWT and internal-key paths, exercised today only end to end by infra/verify/auth-verify.mjs against the VPS.

packages/db-migrations.why: No test script at all, and none is wanted: it is SQL plus a Makefile. The migrations are exercised by applying them — `make migrate-up`, and by the disposable-database run in 3f544b3 that applied all 41 from empty.

services/agent-service.why: 186 files, no unit tests. The riskiest untested code is passport.service.ts and risk-profile.ts, both touched by cb0d4bf, where the level a mandate asks for has to be the level that gets armed. Covered today only by agents-verify.mjs and docs-verify.mjs against a live VPS — which means not covered on a laptop, and not in CI.

services/arca-service.why: 62 files, no unit tests. Holds the payments and entitlement paths, including subscriptions.service.ts from 83b23ea where a payment has to buy the thing the payment is for. Money moves through here, so this is the most expensive gap in this ledger.

services/marketplace.why: 32 files, no unit tests. Listings and subscription discovery; the subscription side is exercised by subscription-verify.mjs and subscription-chain-verify.mjs against real rows and real transactions.

services/web.why: 98 source files, no unit tests and NO TEST SCRIPT AT ALL — `npm test` does not enter this workspace, so it is the one entry here that is not even reached by the runner. It was also missing from this ledger entirely until 2026-09-20, which made `npm test` fail with 'a workspace nobody has decided about is one nobody is measuring'. That failure was correct and it is what put this row here. What covers it instead is infra/verify/web-verify.mjs, which fetches every page server-side and requires the rendered HTML to contain the API's own values IN THE API'S ORDER — 134 checks, and the reason a page that re-sorted a list or printed a zero where the API sent null is caught. The browser pass (infra/verify/browser/browser-check.mjs, signin-verify.mjs) drives the pages in a real browser. Both run against a deployed VPS, so like the other rows here: not covered on a laptop, and not in CI. The specific gap neither reaches is client-component logic that never renders server-side — lib/markdown.tsx is the sharpest example, since it is the one file turning other people's text into markup.
